--- title: "Lexical decision, pseudoword-biased (trisyllabic)" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · LEC_DECLEX_PSEUDO_3sil" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (C · Oral reading fluency; quality class B). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea LEC_DECLEX_PSEUDO_3sil`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Decisión léxica con sesgo a pseudopalabras (trisílabas)*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/LEC_DECLEX_PSEUDO_3sil.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class B.** It has enough data to be described, but it lacks some of the guarantees of class A (stability across time points, item-level reliability or validity). Use with caution and not for individual decisions. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Lexical decision, pseudoword-biased (trisyllabic), from age 6 to 11 (1,780 administrations in 5 cohorts). AUC .83–.84 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 10684 | | Battery | — | | Format | forced choice | | Items | 45 | | Task family | C · Oral reading fluency | | Score | Correct responses per minute | | Instructions (platform) | En esta tarea tienes que responder a ¿?. Si es una palabra, debes pulsar en SI. *(Spanish)* | ![Example of the screen format (2018 screenshot; not necessarily an item from this task).](../../figuras/pantallas/formato_decision.png){width=45%} ## Theoretical framework In lexical decision the child sees a string of letters and decides whether it is a word ("Is this a word?", YES/NO). It measures **visual word recognition**: fast and secure access to the orthographic lexicon. In 2021/22 it was administered to groups, on tablets, in subtests of 45 stimuli of one to four syllables. Some are biased toward words (36 words and 9 pseudowords) and others toward pseudowords (the reverse proportion). The score is efficiency: correct responses per unit of time. **What the evidence says:** - **Children decide by searching their lexicon, not by reading to themselves.** Beginning and advanced readers show length effects, but their orthographic neighborhood effects resemble those of adults and do not change when articulation is blocked. They base the decision on a lexical search [@vandenboer2012lexical]. - **In Spanish, the orthographic lexicon carries weight beyond decoding.** In 1,070 schoolchildren from Grade 2 to Grade 6, lexical orthographic processing contributed to reading competence and became more refined with years of practice [@cuadro2014lexico]. - **The proportion of words and pseudowords shifts the response criterion.** Participants adopt a single criterion that depends on the set of stimuli, not on each trial [@paul1992criterio]. That proportion changes both accuracy and response times [@ratcliff2004diffusion]. With 80% words, a child who always answers "YES" gets 80% right: sensitivity and bias should be separated. - **Group screening on tablets is feasible.** A tablet application given to 616 five-year-olds predicted Grade 1 reading difficulties with a sensitivity of 90% [@zugarramurdi2022lexiland]. **What our data show.** There is one administration per child and school year: there is no stability estimate and no α. - **Validity.** It is the family with the best concurrent validity on the platform. Against persistent difficulty, AUC from .75 to .87 between ages 9 and 11. Against low Woodcock-Muñoz fluency in the same school year, AUC from .66 to .81 (ρ = .30–.58). - **Bias and length.** The versions biased toward words and toward pseudowords perform almost the same. The one-syllable versions, given only at ages 6–7, are the weakest (AUC .56–.74). - **Homographs.** AUC .84–.85 against persistent difficulty and ρ = .59–.69 with Woodcock-Muñoz, the highest relation in the group. Given the instructions, it seems to measure silent sentence reading efficiency more than comprehension of homographs. - **Caution.** At ages 6–7 efficiency is very skewed (extreme values up to 172), and at age 11 the reference group is small (80–102 children). ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 6.2| 2015| 950|2021/22 | 235| 0| 24| 8| | 7.1| 2014| 950|2021/22 | 241| 0| 0| 8| | 9.2| 2012| 949|2021/22 | 388| 76| 0| 11| | 10.2| 2011| 948|2021/22 | 461| 0| 349| 16| | 11.2| 2010| 948|2021/22 | 455| 50| 247| 16| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness|% floor |% ceiling | |----------:|--:|-------:|-----:|-----:|------:|--------:|:-------|:---------| | 9.2| 76| 2012| 27.12| 10.76| 28.45| -0.13|NA |NA | | 11.2| 50| 2010| 40.50| 13.89| 42.73| -0.40|NA |NA | **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct items per minute). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. | Warning| |----------:|--:|:--------------------|:---------|-------:| | 9.2| 76|3.8–49.0 |2.7–50.2 | | | 11.2| 50|7.2–66.0 |4.6–67.2 | | ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Word and text reading (6.2, r = .18); Reading comprehension (7.1, r = .19); Reading comprehension (9.2, r = .15); Word and text reading (10.2, r = .21); Word and text reading (11.2, r = .15). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .83–.84. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_LEC_DECLEX_PSEUDO_3sil_F2_validez.png){width=85%} ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:| | 6.2| 235| 2015| 4.2| 6.0| 7.1| 9.0| 12.9| 17.0| 26.4| | 7.1| 241| 2014| 7.1| 9.3| 10.8| 13.8| 19.1| 26.9| 35.5| | 9.2| 388| 2012| 7.8| 11.1| 16.3| 19.4| 26.6| 34.7| 41.0| | 10.2| 461| 2011| 10.0| 15.8| 20.2| 24.4| 33.4| 43.0| 51.9| | 11.2| 455| 2010| 10.8| 19.7| 24.7| 29.4| 39.3| 48.9| 57.9| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_LEC_DECLEX_PSEUDO_3sil_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|---:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 10.2| 461| -0.047| 0.310| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 10.2| 461| -0.158| 0.089| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 10.2| 459| -0.016| 0.736| |School (ICC) | 10.2| 461| 0.012| | |School SES (ρ) | 11.2| 455| -0.018| 0.700| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 11.2| 452| -0.064| 0.497| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 11.2| 431| 0.030| 0.531| |School (ICC) | 11.2| 455| 0.000| | |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.2| 207| 0.008| 0.956| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.2| 233| -0.007| 0.921| |School (ICC) | 6.2| 235| 0.000| | |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 7.1| 239| -0.093| 0.473| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 7.1| 239| 0.117| 0.070| |School (ICC) | 7.1| 241| 0.063| | |School SES (ρ) | 9.2| 170| 0.206| 0.007| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 9.2| 384| -0.059| 0.569| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 9.2| 384| -0.007| 0.884| |School (ICC) | 9.2| 388| 0.054| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Lexical decision, pseudoword-biased (trisyllabic)” (code 10684) assesses visual word recognition (lexical decision). The child selects a response among the options presented on the screen. It comprises 45 items. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014 and 2015 cohorts it was administered in 6 sessions, from 6 to 11 years of age. The main outcome is the efficiency (correct responses per unit of time). ## Pending issues - Aplicación colectiva en tableta (2021/22). *(Spanish)* - **Dictionary correction.** Corregida el 2026-10-21: antes LEC_PSEUDO_3sil. Catálogo de la plataforma: «Evaluación coles 2021-2022 RV-RF …», consigna «¿ESTO ES UNA PALABRA?» (SÍ/NO). Es una decisión léxica colectiva en tableta (subpruebas de 45 estímulos: 36 palabras y 9 pseudopalabras, o al revés), como la describe el artículo de prevalencia de M. Loredo, no la lectura en voz alta de listas. Máximo observado: 45. *(Spanish)* - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
